scope: Production React and API handlers, exact isolated PostgreSQL migrations; synthetic Auth, REST/Storage transport and deterministic OCR provider

cognitiveLoad.decisions: Instrument choice, with PHQ-9 preselected; score and examination date are clinical values
Document action in the contextual menu; the source file is the required input
Scan action, one uncertain-answer correction in the tested source, final approval (2 choices for a fully legible source)
Scan action, accept the new hospitalization, retain the existing allergy, final approval; decisions scale only with relevant differences
Clinical registration status, with Already taking preselected; medication, dose and frequency are required values

counting: From the relevant tab already open. Action clicks count menu opening, action choice, native file-picker opening and Save/Approve; typing, field focus, native file selection and correction controls are separate. Decision counts include workflow selections and clinical approval judgments in the tested scenario, including preselected instrument/status choices; typing known clinical values is counted under fields. Source upload/review states stay within one dialog.
limitations: Live OpenAI OCR was replaced by a deterministic provider response.
Supabase-owned Auth/REST/object byte transport was emulated; exact application migrations, RPCs and RLS executed in isolated PGlite PostgreSQL.
Native PDF rendering is unavailable in the local headless browser. Authorized original PDF bytes and compact fallback links were verified; the original PNG questionnaire rendered visibly.
No production database, real clinical data, external email or SMS was used.
finalRefinement: Desktop and mobile existing-patient workflow rerun after limiting the individual measurement chart to 480px, shortening the results disclosure, clarifying the manual-score action, and defensively treating historical measurements as unlinked.
